headlines.text: Turning the clock back to 2023: gold changed shoulders as the AEW Women's World Title found a new champion as Hikaru Shida vs. Toni Storm battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 7.13 ? a strong outing ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. It marked Toni Storm's 10th match with the title on the line. On the 200th episode of Dynamite, Shida overcame interference from Storm's Outcasts stablemates and reversed a Storm Zero pin attempt into her own rollup to become a two-time AEW Women's World Champion.
Looking back to 2024, when MxM Collection vs. Private Party locked horns for the first time, serving as the night's main event on Rampage, rated 6.06.

Turning the clock back to 2023: Aussie Open vs. Komander & Vikingo fought tooth and nail for the ROH World Tag Team Titles, appearing on Dynamite, rated 7.29 ? a good, competitive contest. For Komander & Vikingo, it marked a first real shot at championship gold. Every title match carries a little extra weight, and this one was no exception.

secondaries.text: On this day in 2023, Jericho & Takeshita stepped through the curtain for the first time as a team, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.31.
That Wednesday in 2023, Trent Beretta vs. Jon Moxley vs. Penta El Zero M fought it out in an Anything Goes match on Dynamite, rated 7.82 ? a well-worked match in a hard-fought men's division clash.
Looking back to 2023, when The Elite vs. Jarrett, Lethal & Singh met for the very first time on Dynamite, rated 6.50.
